caseno: Appeal from Original Order No. 321 of 2000 with Civil Rule No.483 (fm) of 2000
lawyer:
SK Siddique, Advocate ----- For the Appellant. 
Shafique Ahmed with Kazi Kamrul Alam, Advocates ----- For the Respondent
parties:
Abdul Mannan Miah  ----- Appellant
Vs.
Md Salaiman Miah  ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Tafazzul Islam J: The appellant preferred this First Miscellaneous Appeal challenging the judgment and order dated 6-6-2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Kishoreganj, in Title Suit No. 3 of 1999 allowing the application of the plaintiff respondent filed under Order XXXIX rules 1 and 2 CPC and also rejecting the application of the defendant appellant filed under Order VII rule 11 CPC. 

 2. The plaintiff, the proprietor of Zakir Soap Factory, filed the aforesaid Title Suit No. 3 of 1999 praying for an order of permanent injunction restraining the defendant from producing and distributing soap containing the trade mark Ghadi stating, inter alia, that the trade mark Ghari with the device clock was being used by the plaintiff since long in respect of washing soaps falling in class III manufactured by Zakir Soap Factory and the said registration of trade mark Ghari with device clock registered in the name of Zakir Soap Factory has been renewed by the Trade Mark Registry for a period of 15 years with effect from 22nd May, 1992, and so the said registration is valid till the year 2007 and that the people of Bangladesh are quite familiar with Trade Mark Ghari and Clock device owned by the plaintiff and thus the plaintiff has acquired the very valuable reputation in respect of the said Trade Mark. The plaintiff has also incurred huge expenditure towards publicity of the said trade mark Ghari with clock device through various media and a result of its extensive use and publicity of a long time for sale of the soap produced by it, the said trade mark has become distinctive mark of the products of the plaintiff in Bangladesh and it has now come to such a stage that any product with the similar trade mark of the opponent will at once denote to the public .that the said products or products have emanated from the plaintiff. But the defendant, with full knowledge of the fact that Ghari and clock device has acquired fame and reputation throughout Bangladesh, with a view to capitalise on such goodwill and reputation of the plaintiff in respect of the aforesaid trade mark Ghari and clock device started producing and distributing soap by using similar trade mark Ghadi and device which is similar and identical to Ghari and clock device of the plaintiff thus encroaching upon the rights of the plaintiff and to lead the public into believing that the goods manufactured by the defendant emanate from the plaintiff and that same class of purchase of the soap both with trade mark Ghari and Ghadi will be available at the same shops and counters and soaps will be sold to the same class of purchasers as the channels of trade of both the plaintiff and the defendants are same. Since the defendants are passing off their goods in place of the genuine goods of the plaintiff, decree of permanent injunction is passed restraining the defendants from producing and marketing soaps by using the similar design, colour and packet of the trade mark of the plaintiff for the soap manufactured by the plaintiff. 

 3. On the very date of the filing of the suit ie on 1-9-99, the plaintiff also filed an application under Order XXXIX rule 1 CPC praying for an order of temporary injunction to the above effect. Then show because notice was also issued on 1-9-99. 

 4. As it appears from the records the plaintiff in support of their claim filed Trade Mark Registration No. 31239 dated 28-8-90, Patent and Design Registration Certificate dated, 4-6-95, Design and Registration certificate dated 7-5-95, Registration of Trade Mark No. 22202 dated 19-2-92, Registration of Copyright No. 5252 dated 7-5-95, BSTI certificate dated 18-8-99, Notice of caution and legal notice dated 20-7-99. 

 5. The defendant apart from fling an application under Order VII, rule 11 CPC praying for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the suit is barred by the Rules framed under the Patent and Design Act 1911 and Trade Marks Act, also filed written objection against the application for temporary injunction stating, inter alia, that since the trade mark of the plaintiff has not been registered, he is not entitled to get any relief under section 21 of the Trade Marks Act, 1940 and the suit is also not maintainable under section 20(2) of the aforesaid Act. Further, the defendant has applied to the Trade Mark Registry for registration of their Trade Mark Ghadi, the number of the application is 60790 dated 18-7-99, and the plaintiff may oppose the same under section 15 of the Trade Marks Act, 1940, so the suit being premature is liable to be dismissed and further since the Registrar in terms of section 10(2) of the Trade Marks Act may pass appropriate order for registration of trade' mark in the name of different persons, the suit as well as application for injunction cannot proceed. Further, since there is no similarity between the two proceedings, the defendant cannot be debarred from using the trades mark Ghadi under section 22 of the Trade Marks Act even if the trades mark of the plaintiff Ghari was registered earlier. In fact, the defendant was producing soap with trade mark Ghadi in their factory since 18-7-99 and so if the defendant gets registration the same will be effective from 18-7-99. Before starting production, the defendant on 30-6-99 also submitted declaration to Board of Revenue for fixing the VAT. The plaintiff, being jealous of the sale and popularity of the soap containing trade mark Ghadi, has filed an application for registration of trade mark Ghari for the soap produced by them. Further, there is also no similarity between the plaintiffs Ghari and defendants Ghadi and the design, colour, etc. of these are completely different and so there is no scope of any confusion among the public regarding the two products and the defendants never committed any breach of the trade mark. 

 6. The defendant in support of their claim filed search report No. 4540 of 1999 dated 7-6-99 regarding Ghari Mark, the application for registration which is No. 60790 dated 18-7-99 along with papers showing marketing of washing soap Ghadi since 1-7-99, legal notice date 20-7-99 issued on behalf of the plaintiff, declaration of VAT at dated 30-6-99, Challan of VAT dated 1-7-99, renewed Trade Licence dated 11-8-99 certificate showing that the defendant No.1 is a member of Bhairab Chamber of Commerce and his membership No. 55, the poster advertising washing soap with trade mark Ghadi, the advertisement dated 20-8-99, regarding trade mark, the GD dated 8-8-92 filed by the defendant No. 1 with Bhariab PS. 

 8. Mr SK Siddique, the learned Advocate for the appellant. submits that there is no similarity between trademarks Ghari and Ghadi and that the trade mark of the defendant appellant has been advertised in the Trade Mark Journal, and the Trade Mark Registry after considering the objection filed by the plaintiff has granted registration of the trade mark Ghadi and thereby this suit became infructuous and accordingly, the order of temporary injunction is liable to be set aside, and further since the Registrar of Trade Mark, being competent to decide the dispute, granted registration to the defendant considering the merit of the application and so the infringement if any also ceased. Mr Siddique lastly submits that the remedy of the plaintiff, if any, lies by filing appeal in the High Court Division and having failed to do so the impugned order is also liable to be set aside. 

 9. Mr Shafique Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff and on the said date the application for injunction was also filed by respondent. submits that the suit was filed on 1-9-99 and that the impugned order of temporary injunction was passed on 6-6-2000 in terms of show cause notice dated 1-9-99, whereas the registration of Trade Mark Ghadi was given on 17-10-2000 ie long after passing of the order of temporary injunction and this appeal is the continuation of the said proceeding of injunction and so this court while deciding this appeal will not take into consideration the registration granted on 17-10-2000. Mr Ahmed relying on the decision reported in 48 DLR 228, 50 DLR 548, 1987 BLD (AD) 130, PLD 1973 Karachi 289, PLD 1983 Karachi 367, AIR 1962 AP 510, and 1984 SCMR 1024 next submits that deception is the test and the packet of the trade mark Ghadi being similar to Ghari will confuse the purchasers of the soap with trade mark Ghari, and the defendant appellant with malafide motive, started production and marketing of the soap using the trade mark Ghadi and so the learned Subordinate Judge having found that the plaintiff showed a prima facie case and the balance of convenience and inconvenience is also in favour of the plaintiff, rightly passed the order of temporary injunction during the pendency of the application for registration. Mr Ahmed lastly, submits that even subsequent registration of trade mark Ghadi cannot be a ground against passing off and the implication of section 25 of the Trade Mark Act is that, so the party who got registration later cannot file suit for registration and so the plaintiff who obtained registration earlier, can sue the defendant for infringement but vis-a-vis the defendant is not allowed to file suit for infringement in view of section 25. 

 11. As it appears from the contents of the impugned order, the learned Additional District Judge found that the trade mark Ghari had been Registered as Trade Mark No. 22202 and 31329 in class-3 in the name of Zakir Soap Factory and the same has been renewed on 19-2-92 for a period of 15 years from 22-5-92, and the plaintiff also got copyright registration in respect of trade mark Ghari and further the learned Additional District Judge after comparing the colour ,design and packet of the soaps using trademarks Ghari and Ghadi could not also find any significant difference. In the application dated 26-7-2000 filed in the Civil Rule No. 483(fm) of 2000 praying for vacating the order of stay the said memo of Renewal No. 1716/92 dated 19-2-92, the trade mark of soap Ghadi which has also been approved by BSTI and also the cover of the soap using the trade mark Ghadi have been enclosed and during hearing I compared the covers of soaps using trade mark Ghari and Ghadi but could not also find any significant difference, and so as it appears there is possibility of passing off. In the decisions reported in 48 DLR 28, 50 DLR 548, 1987 BW (AD) 130 (and 28 DLR 1171) it has been held that in case of passing off, the civil Court may pass decree for permanent injunction. 

 13. In the case of Abdul Jabbar vs Ahmed Jan reported in PLD 1973 Karachi 289. the plaintiff, the proprietor of the registered trade mark in respect of bidi described as Kohinoor Bidi 505, filed suit for praying for permanent Injunction alleging infringement against the defendant who introduced bidis with the name and mark Kohi Noor Bidi 506 in wrapper identical in colour, design and get-up as that of plaintiffs registered trade mark. The trial Court found substantial resemblance in material respect likely to deceive or cause confusion in the minds of unwary purchasers and accordingly, passed order of temporary injunction restraining defendant from infringing plaintiffs trade mark even though the application for registration filed by the defendant before the Trade Mark Registry was pending. On appeal Karachi High Court upheld the order of temporary injunction passed by the trial Court holding that the defendants cannot be allowed to take advantage of their own wrong and the prayer of injunction restraining infringement of trade mark is not to be refused merely because the defendant has applied for registration of his mark. 

 14. In the case of Bumeys Industrial and Commercial Co. Ltd vs Rahman Match Works reported in PLD 1983 Karachi 357, the plaintiff filed suit praying for permanent injunction on the ground of infringement and Karachi High Court held that defendant's trade mark on its match box although carrying several dissimilarities with the plaintiffs trade mark on their match box, yet an unwary purchaser is likely to be misled or deceived in believing that what he is buying is plaintiffs match box due to the resemblance between the two as to cause deception in his mind and accordingly, though the defendant further pleaded that they had applied for registration of their own mark and they were waiting for its registration, decreed the suit and granted order of permanent injunction as prayed. 

 15. In the decision reported in 50 DLR 548 the plaintiff-respondent Social Marketing Company after obtaining registration of the trade mark Orsalin since 1983, started marketing the same since 1983 and the defendant-appellant, Universal Pharmaceutical Ltd on the basis of provisional registration obtained on 5-8-93, started marketing and selling similar product with the name and trade mark Oral saline from the last part of 1983 in spite of the order passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Pabna, in Other Suit No.1 of 1994 for maintaining status quo in respect of marketing and selling of the products of both the parties. The Social Marketing Company filed Title Suit No. 22 of 1995 praying for permanent injunction restraining Universal Pharmaceuticals Ltd from marketing and selling their products using the trade mark Oralsaline and on their prayer, an order of ad interim order of injunction was granted on 1-4-95 restraining Universal Pharmaceutical Ltd from marketing and selling their products, Oralsaline, and on 14-10-95 after hearing the said order of ad interim injunction was made absolute, Being aggrieved, Universal Pharmaceutical Ltd filed appeal and the High Court Division, even though found that Universal Pharmaceutical Ltd obtained provisional registration on 5-8-93, dismissed the appeal holding that using the name of Oralsaline is a clear case of passing off. 

 19. In the case of Berlei vs Bali reported in (1970) RPC 469 the defendants had been the registered proprietors of the mark Bali but this was expunged by the order of the House of Lords on the grounds that it offended against section 11. The defendants thereupon sought to register the mark under the provisions of section 12(2) and at the same time the plaintiffs pressed their action for infringement which had been commenced earlier. Megarry J, refused a stay, observing that a stay should only be granted where the interests of justice (taking into account the claims of both parties) required it. If an injunction were obtained in the action and the defendants subsequently were registered and thus obtained the protection of section 4(4) the injunction could be qualified ab initio or varied when registration was effected. 

 22. In the decision reported in 1984 SCMR 1024, as it appears, the petitioner claimed proprietary right on the trade mark Arminous registered in their favour on 16-8-66 and since renewed for 15 years from 6-8-73 and the respondent No. 1 who is also a trader of arms and ammunition, imported 105 revolvers bearing trade mark Arminous which remained in the custody of customs authority. The petitioner while filing the suit for permanent injunction for restraining the respondent No. 1 for using the trade mark Arminous also filed an application praying for granting temporary injunction to the above effect but the said application was rejected by the trial Court on 16-11-93 on the ground that the petitioner had not established a prima facie case. The petitioner then filed an appeal before the High Court and filed an application in the said appeal praying for ad interim relief but the said application was dismissed holding that the documentary evidence produced before the trial Court showed that arms bearing trade mark Arminous had been imported in Pakistan by different dealers prior to 1966 when the trade mark was registered in the name of the petitioner and so the petitioner had no prima facie Case. The petitioner moved Pakistan Supreme Court and at the time of hearing before the Supreme Court both sides wanted to produce some new documents but the Supreme Court held that since the court was examining the correctness of the decision of the trial Court on the basis of document which had been produced before the said court, it would not be proper to advert to any new document, and the Supreme Court dismissed the petition on the ground that the document on record would not fully establish that the German firm, the original owner of the Trade Mark, have abandoned all its rights in the trade mark in favour of the petitioner in Pakistan. 

 23. So, this court while disposing this First Miscellaneous Appeal is to consider as to whether the plaintiff had a prima facie case at the time of filing of the suit and this court should not take into consideration the registration of the trade mark Ghadi made on 17-2-2000 ie after institution of the suit and it is the trial Court who will decide as to whether the registration was proper or not. 

 24. Further, the contention that in view of the registration of the trade mark Ghadi Title Suit No. 3 of 1999 has been made infructuous cannot also be considered at this stage of hearing of the application for injunction because the question of maintainability of the suit has to be decided at the time of trial and not at the time of hearing of the temporary injunction. The court at the time of hearing of the temporary injunction will only consider whether petitioner has a prima facie case, whether the balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the petitioner and whether the petitioner will suffer irreparable loss and injury if injunction is not granted. 

 28. In view of the above and the fact that the learned Subordinate Judge found that the plaintiff has a prima facie case the balance of convenience and inconvenience was also in favour of the plaintiff, I am of the view that the learned Court did not commit. any illegality in passing the impugned order.
